scientific_question: How should SupCon and/or domain-generalization losses be designed, staged, smoke-tested, and interpreted so the next controlled run directly targets subject variability and remains scientifically diagnosable?
authorized_scope: Read project docs and scripts to recover existing SupCon/DG design notes.
Define smoke tests before any performance run.
Define a small controlled hyperparameter plan, not a broad search.
Define decision logic for interpreting success/failure.

design_decisions_to_lock.required_decision: Use subject-relative q33 labels initially or justify another label policy.
Define same-task/same-class positives, with cross-subject positives required when feasible.
Define opposite-class negatives and hard negatives, including same-stimulus/different-label cases if available.
Guarantee each contrastive batch contains enough subjects and class diversity for valid positives/negatives.
Define subject as environment for VREx/DG or justify a coarser fold/task environment.
Choose CE+SupCon, CE+VREx, or CE+SupCon+VREx first-pass; specify weights and warmup.
Define candidate ranges for temperature, SupCon weight, VREx weight, projection dimension, batch size, warmup, and optimizer/lr; specify which are smoke-only versus first-pass ablations.
Define sampler integrity, leakage guard, micro-overfit, shuffled-label negative control, and minimal fold/task smoke gates.
Keep first pass minimal and diagnostic; specify run count, metrics, and pass/fail criteria.
All preprocessing/scaling and sampler construction must respect train/validation separation.
Define what to conclude if smoke fails, if embeddings align but macro-F1 does not improve, or if VREx reduces risk variance without performance gain.

preliminary_hyperparameter_registry_to_r.grid_policy: Do not run full Cartesian grid in first pass; choose a small staged matrix after smoke tests.

required_smoke_tests.name: pair_sampler_integrity_smoke
required_smoke_tests.purpose: Verify every contrastive batch has valid positives/negatives and enough subjects/classes.

required_smoke_tests.name: leakage_guard_smoke
required_smoke_tests.purpose: Verify preprocessing/scaling and pair selection do not use validation labels/features improperly.

required_smoke_tests.name: supcon_micro_overfit_smoke
required_smoke_tests.purpose: Verify CE+SupCon can overfit a tiny train-only subset and loss decreases.

required_smoke_tests.name: shuffled_label_negative_control
required_smoke_tests.purpose: Verify contrastive setup does not produce meaningful performance on shuffled labels.

required_smoke_tests.name: one_fold_one_task_minimal_smoke
required_smoke_tests.purpose: Run one task/fold/config only after integrity tests pass.
required_smoke_tests.failure_interpretation: Use embedding diagnostics to decide if loss, sampler, or task signal is failing.

pass_criteria: Spec must cite and summarize existing project SupCon/DG design notes found in docs/scripts.
Spec must state exactly whether SupCon, VREx/DG, or both are selected for first pass.
Spec must define subject-aware sampler constraints.
Spec must define smoke tests before training.
Spec must define a small staged hyperparameter plan, not a broad search.
Spec must define VREx/DG environment rules.
Spec must provide a minimal first-pass run matrix.
Spec must update docs/project_status_current.md and docs/project_status_current.json.
next_allowed_step: Search/read existing project docs and scripts, then generate the cautious SupCon/DG design spec with smoke tests and hyperparameter registry.
